one_liner: Look up a precise, cross-linked definition for any term used anywhere in the LLM stack.

key_terms.definition: Per-layer, per-token storage of key/value matrices from prior tokens, avoiding recomputation during autoregressive decoding; grows with sequence length and batch size.
Core Transformer operation where each token forms a softmax-normalized, scaled dot-product weighted sum over other tokens' value vectors.
Three-stage pipeline (SFT, reward model training, PPO fine-tuning) that aligns model behavior with human preferences using a learned reward signal.
PEFT technique adding a trainable low-rank decomposition ΔW=BA to frozen weight matrices, cutting trainable parameters 10-1000×.
IO-aware attention algorithm that tiles QKV into SRAM and fuses softmax with matmul, avoiding materializing the full N×N attention matrix.
Architecture where each block holds N expert FFN sub-networks and a learned router activates only k << N per token, scaling parameters cheaply.
Empirical power-law relationships linking model size, dataset size, compute, and test loss, used to predict optimal training configurations (e.g., Chinchilla).
Pattern that injects retrieved context from a vector database or search engine into the prompt to ground generation without retraining.
Latency-reduction technique where a small draft model proposes K tokens that a large target model verifies in one parallel forward pass.
vLLM's virtual-page KV-cache management scheme enabling near-zero memory fragmentation and cross-request prefix sharing.
Prompting technique eliciting step-by-step intermediate reasoning before a final answer, improving accuracy on multi-step tasks.
Attention variant where h query heads share g < h key-value heads, cutting KV-cache size by h/g versus standard multi-head attention.
